topics.title: Noble's walk-through
topics.intro: From Noble's walk-through (2026-10-15) and your notes after it: 102 points in docs/comp-report/feedback/2026-10-15-noble/, one report per topic, and Dispatches 15–24. Each question has a recommended default, so the dispatches build on it unless you object. Read the topic reports alongside: each question cites its NW ids.

questions.q: Where do the six tags outside Noble's four groups go?
questions.context:
What this is about. No outdoor space, 6+ months, Full service, Renovated, Water views and New development fit none of Noble's groups (NW-045).

Why it needs you. The server rejects a tag no longer on the list, so renaming or dropping one needs a data migration. Keeping every current string avoids it.
options: Similarities for Full service, Renovated, Water views, New development; a "Differences" group for No outdoor space and 6+ months
Drop the ones a feature or check already says
needs a migration of stored tags

questions.q: Should the five-row price table also go in the email?
questions.context:
What this is about. The price table on Findings runs 10 to 12 rows and confused Noble. The replacement is five rows (low, three inner points, high) plus a calculator (NW-065).

Why it needs you. The email uses the same rows today (Frankie's full steps). One table everywhere is easier to explain, and the writer and QA then check what the agent saw.
options: Five rows on Findings and in the email
Five on Findings, the full steps in the email
Five everywhere, full steps behind a "more rows" link on Findings

questions.q: Should Hubert see the agent's own number and the target after the reveal?
questions.short: Hubert sees the target and your call
questions.context:
What this is about. D-4 said Hubert sees the target once the result is shown. The build never shows it (NW-068, NW-093). The fix is a new prompt version. The numbers are computed without the target either way, and the writer stays blind.

Why it needs you. D-4 covers only the target. The agent sees their own Gate number beside the estimate, and Hubert could use it to explain the gap.
options: read-only; never in the email or the writer

questions.q: Whose number is the target by default?
questions.context:
What this is about. A new toggle says whose the target is: client, agent or both (NW-070). The label follows it.

Why it needs you. The field already reads as the client's hope, and Noble read it that way.

questions.q: Pre-approval: yes or no, or yes or no plus the amount?
questions.context:
What this is about. The client fields (NW-074) add financing (cash or mortgage) and pre-approval.

Why it needs you. The amount caps what a buyer can offer, which is what Noble used to argue his all-cash offer. It costs one optional field.
options: Yes or no, plus the amount

questions.q: Which good email is the example, and who writes it?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble wants a good email agents can look at (NW-085). It later serves Sort notes and headlines too.

Why it needs you. It sets the bar for Casa's voice. The Barclay sample uses the engine's own numbers; Noble approves the voice. It needs the writer's real eval run, which waits on TD-3's key.
options: The 100 Barclay sample, drafted by the writer, edited by Noble
You write one by hand against the sample's numbers

questions.q: May an agent mark a report as sent without using the Copy button?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble could not reach Done (NW-086). Mark as sent only turns on after a copy through the button. A hand copy from the textarea never does.

Why it needs you. Allowing it changes a rule you set. The copy log would still record only real copies.
options: Yes, Mark as sent always works
No, a button copy comes first

questions.q: What may Hubert write on the platform?
questions.context:
What this is about. Hubert is read-only now. You want him to see what the agent sees and maybe act (NW-093).

Why it needs you. D-27 item 6 says he never tiers, writes notes or picks tags. B keeps that and still gives him real ability. C weakens the notes, which are the agent's own learning. The confirmation card goes to Claude Design.
options: Propose and confirm: home and comp facts, features, putting a removed export row back, email fixes
B plus proposing tags and notes

questions.q: Who writes "How Hubert got there"?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble found it dense (NW-063). Today it is built in code from the engine's output, not by a model.

Why it needs you. Every figure must come from the engine, the screen is opened constantly, and a model call adds cost and delay. An "Ask Hubert about this" chip can open the drawer instead.

What it blocks. Dispatch 21 item 1 builds on A; B moves the item to Calliste.
options: Hubert's live words from a model call

questions.q: Does the writer move to Calliste, the new AI track?
questions.context:
What this is about. You defined Calliste as owner of all AI prompts, tools and context (NW-093 a). It takes Hubert. The writer (Dispatch 13 phase 2) is also a Claude call with a prompt and an eval.

Why it needs you. Splitting AI work across two tracks recreates the problem Calliste is for. Mason keeps Send UI, QA and fair-housing. Calliste starts after the account move.
options: Yes, Calliste owns the writer's prompts and eval
No, the writer stays with Mason

questions.q: Should deal terms (seller target, price, rate, down payment) reach Hubert after the reveal?
questions.context:
What this is about. They are kept out today as a seller's target is a deal term (NW-068).

Why it needs you. Decide with the client fields (NW-074) so privacy and the fair-housing limits are set once.
options: Include them after the reveal, same rule as the target

questions.q: How should sessions read production data?
questions.context:
What this is about. You want Claude sessions to see what happens in production (NW-090). The rule today is that sessions never connect to the production database.

Why it needs you. A key-gated inspection API keeps the rule. It is read-only at the database (its own select-only actor), returns named views with client text redacted, and shows client text only for one report at a time, logged before it returns, at most 20 an hour. A separate test key lets a session write, but only as a test user, and copies of real reports are always redacted. A read-only database role is better for ad hoc SQL but breaks the rule. A needs four settings (TD-14) and runs from Casa's account only (Dispatch 23 items 3–4).
options: redacted by default; text on request, logged

questions.q: Should mentors see every agent's report, or only their own agents'?
questions.context:
What this is about. Admins can open any report by link, but only the owner's reports are listed, and mentors are admitted nowhere (NW-088).

Why it needs you. There are two or three mentors; assignment needs someone to maintain it, and we don't build on agent responsiveness. Agents would be told in their welcome copy that mentors can read their reports. Until then: open Noble's report from its ?report= link.

What it holds. Deploying Dispatch 22a gives every mentor read access to every report, so Casanova holds 22a's merge until you answer. B changes one rule, in two places. The sign-in fix (22 item 2) can ship on its own first.

questions.q: Who may start and reset a sample report?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble and Kara review flows and can't use the sample today (NW-054). A co-op sample is added.

Why it needs you. Replies and Hubert's transcript can't be deleted, so a truly clean reset means a new report from the same code and the old one archived (new link).

Until you answer, the server keeps samples admin-only. A widens it to mentors (Dispatch 23 items 1–2).
options: Admins and mentors; reset replaces the report
Admins only; reset replaces the report
Admins and mentors; try an in-place reset

questions.q: When do the Phase A dispatches start, given the move to Casa's Claude account?
questions.short: Dispatch before or after the move
questions.context:
What this is about. Sessions can't move between Claude accounts (NW-096). Mason, Abacus and Surveyor already run in this account; they can take Dispatches 15–22 now and restart in the Casa account later from kickoffs, as they did on 2026-10-13. A new track (Calliste, Dispatch 24) and anything that holds a production key (Dispatch 23) start in the Casa account.

Why it needs you. Starting now gets the build moving while you design; holding everything costs about a week.
options: Running tracks start now; new tracks and production keys wait for the Casa account

questions.q: How do we record the next walk-through?
questions.context:
What this is about. The last walk-through wasn't recorded; the dictation is all we have (NW-097).

Why it needs you. It costs nothing to record on your own machine. The activity log (NW-099) only shows what Noble did, not what he said.
options: Record on your machine (screen and mic)
Upgrade the Meet host seat to one with recording
activity log and notebook notes only

questions.q: A rental-comps report: wanted, and when?
questions.context:
What this is about. Noble comped rentals for a client buying to rent out (NW-021). Today the tool warns when a pasted link is a rental, which he liked. A rental-comps report would take rentals and warn on sales instead, and needs the engine to price rents: a new report kind.

Why it needs you. It's a real use, but not the pilot's core. Today's gate stays either way.
options: Later: after the pilot's sales flow settles
Soon: investor clients are part of the pilot

questions.q: Create the email as a Gmail draft, for Casa Workspace accounts?
questions.context:
What this is about. NW-102. A Google Cloud project under Casa's Workspace, its OAuth consent set to Internal, asks Casa users once for Gmail's compose permission (no Google app review for internal apps). On "Create Gmail draft" the browser gets a short-lived token and puts the Designed email straight into the agent's Drafts, built exactly as it should arrive: no paste problems (left-aligned, italic, blue links). No Gmail tokens stored. Casa Workspace accounts only; personal Gmail keeps Copy. The same Casa Google client also lets Workspace trust the comp report's Google sign-in (Noble's refusal).

Why it needs you. You create the project and client in Casa's Workspace admin (a checklist comes with the dispatch). Build is Phase B.
options: Yes: set up the Casa Google client, build it in Phase B
Not now: Copy stays the only way

topics.title: The comp report
topics.intro: The comp report is priority one. These come from D-25 and D-17, from the writer's PR (#76) and from Jev's PR (#56).

questions.q: Who reviews the fair-housing list?
questions.context:
What this is about. The writer's QA has one hard block: compliance (D-2). A term on the hard list blocks Copy outright ("adults only", "perfect for young professionals", "no Section 8", "school district", "safe neighborhood"). A word on the near list ("family", "church", "school") warns, and the agent acknowledges it before copying.

Why it needs you. Mason drafted the list from HUD's advertising guidance and New York City's Human Rights Law ({repo}/tools-src/comp-report/workspace/fair-housing.ts, version fh-2026-10-14). A list that blocks agents' emails needs a reviewer before the pilot widens.

questions.q: "Appraisal contingency": keep it blocked, or allow it as a deal term?
questions.context:
What this is about. "Appraisal" in client copy is a hard block (design §9.3), because a comp email must never read as an appraisal. So an agent who writes about waiving the appraisal contingency in the next step can't copy the email.

Why it needs you. The phrase is a normal deal term in a buyer's offer. Allowing it means one exception in the list; keeping it means agents rephrase.
options: Allow the phrase as a deal term

questions.q: Does the writer's house voice read right?
questions.context:
What this is about. Claude now drafts the headlines and the email's sections in Casa's voice, in Frankie's order. The voice is a short style file: plain words, specific comparisons, numbers only from the comps, one to three lines a comp. It's quoted in full in #76's description ({repo}/tools-src/comp-report/server/house-voice.ts).

Why it needs you. It's Casa's voice in front of clients. The real eval drafts (100 Barclay and Frankie's #517) come once CR_EVAL_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is in the cloud environment (TD-3); read them together if you'd rather.
options: Wait for the eval drafts first

questions.q: Jev's seven questions: go with them as written?
questions.context:
What this is about. Jev answers seven fixed questions about each listing's text (sponsor sale, estate sale, tenant in place and the like). The wording is at the end of #56's description. Phase 2 goes live on the reviewed text.

Why it needs you. Casanova read them and found nothing to change. A change after the labelled batch runs means running it again.

questions.q: The ±3 floor band and the ½-mile distance flag most comps. What now?
questions.short: Floor band and distance thresholds: keep?
questions.context:
What this is about. The floor band (±3, from Frankie's email) flags 8 of Hannah's 11 comps; Kara's ½ mile flags 6 of the sample's 11, five of them Primary. A flag is a prompt to the agent, never a block.

Why it needs you. Noble sets or confirms them. Until he does, the numbers stand.
options: Keep them until Noble weighs in
say to what in the note

questions.q: Counsel's two questions: who do they go to, and when?
questions.context:

options: Hold until the pilot is near
Send them to a closing attorney now
